The Buddha's concept of anatta does not mean that we lack an empirical self or a conventional 'I'. He wasn't talking about denying that. The empirical self, our self-image, and our very being are normal, and he did not refute them. He only meant that the 'self' he was critiquing was the 'self' from the Hindu tradition, known as Atman.

mt_en: Where does Mom keep her money, I wonder? Wow, just then, I found a hint in the song. I decided that just this once in my life, I would violate the moral code my teacher taught me. That evening, I went home, waited for my parents to fall asleep, went into the wardrobe where I'd seen Mom hide her money, and took 50,000. Then the next day, I went to school. I felt fancy, I felt incredibly glamorous, and why? I had money.

I'd like to dedicate this song to my exes, to say that
If you still haven't found peace with your new partner,
I hope you will forgive the mistreatment I inflicted,
And that someone is willing to do for you the things I never dared to do.

Perhaps the only credit I have is when it's on my bank card.

mt_en: Japanese cuisine is known for its grilled dishes prepared directly at the table, allowing diners to adjust the doneness of the meat to their liking. Today, Happy Lunch Restaurant will introduce a very characteristic dish from the Land of the Rising Sun: Japanese grilled meat. Ingredients include beef and accompanying grilled vegetables. mt_en: Recently, Dutch artist Florentijn Hofman, famous for his work Rubber Duck, also known as the giant yellow duck, unveiled a new artwork, HippopoThames. The 21-meter-long wooden hippopotamus floats on the River Thames in London, England, marking the opening of the Totally Thames festival. The month-long event features numerous cultural, artistic, and community music activities taking place along the River Thames. Famous for his giant yellow duck that has traveled to many countries worldwide, including Vietnam, this is the first time Dutch artist Hofman has introduced a giant hippopotamus artwork to the British public. The hippopotamus figure is also inspired by the early history of the River Thames, when hippopotamuses once roamed along this river. mt_en: Nanami Nagura, a Japanese artist, has become the new champion of the International Air Guitar Championship, held in Oulu, Finland last weekend. The 18-year-old air guitarist had to overcome competitors from nine other countries, including the US, Germany, the UK, and Canada, to become the 19th champion, with a handmade electric guitar as the prize. The runner-up position went to American champion Matt Burns, followed by 2013 former world champion Aaron Merlin, also from the US. Air guitar is a rather unique discipline where players use hand movements, jumps, and even pretend to sing, while playing an imaginary electric guitar. The winner must command the stage and make the invisible guitar look real. The competition is organized to promote world peace, because you cannot harm anyone with an imaginary guitar in your hands, and wars would not happen if everyone spent their time playing air guitar. According to the official website of the competition.

mt_en: Recently, Dutch artist Florentijn Hofman, famous for his work Rubber Duck, also known as the giant yellow duck, unveiled his new work, Hippopotamus on the Thames. The 21-meter-long wooden hippopotamus was floated on the River Thames in London, England, marking the opening of the Totally Thames festival. The month-long event features numerous cultural, artistic, and community music activities taking place along the River Thames. Famous for his yellow duck that has traveled to many countries around the world, including Vietnam, this is the first time Dutch artist Hofman has unveiled a giant hippopotamus artwork to the British public. The hippopotamus imagery is also inspired by the early history of the River Thames, when hippos once lived along this river. The Hippopotamus on the Thames artwork will be on display until the end of September.

Air guitar is a rather unique discipline where players use hand movements, dance, and even pretend to sing, playing an imaginary electric guitar. The winner must command the stage and make the invisible guitar look real. The competition is held to promote world peace, as you cannot harm anyone with an imaginary guitar in your hands, and war would not happen if everyone spent their time playing air guitar.
